fact_sheet.business_description: Occidental is a US-centered oil and gas producer with interests in chemicals and midstream operations [D01]. The company is the largest acreage holder in the Permian Basin and operates globally with assets in the Rockies, Gulf of Mexico, Oman, Algeria, and the UAE [D01].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Oil and gas produced at 1.17 million boe/d [D01].
Chlorine and caustic soda produced by OxyChem, the largest US merchant producer [D01].
economics: Company cash flow breaks even at approximately $40 WTI including sustaining capital and common dividend [D01].
Permian well costs fell ~30% from 2019 to 2021 [D01].
earnings_record: Earnings are highly cyclical due to commodity price dependence [D02, D05].
competitive_position: Largest acreage holder in the Permian Basin [D01].
Largest US merchant producer of chlorine and caustic soda [D01].
Peer set includes Exxon Mobil, Chevron, and ConocoPhillips [D06].
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Total debt was $29.0 billion at year-end 2021 [D01, D02].
Management goal is to reduce net debt toward $20 billion [D01].
Inherited significant acquisition obligations from 2019 [D03, D07].
management_and_capital_allocation: Capital allocation priorities: 1) Debt reduction to $20bn, 2) $3bn share repurchase authorization and dividend, 3) modest production growth [D01].

yields_pct.basis: Trailing earnings yield based on $1.58 diluted EPS [D04]. FCF yield of 18.5% based on cash-statement FCF of $7.56bn [D04]. Dividend yield based on $0.13/quarter run rate [D04]. Long bond yield is 10-year Treasury [D04].

what_the_market_is_worried_about: War-related oil strength may be temporary [D05].
High commodity prices may encourage uneconomic drilling or acquisitions [D05].
Preferred claims consume cash before common dividends [D05].
deal_terms_if_any: Preferred stock and warrants issued in 2019 for Anadarko acquisition financing [D07].
berkshire_context: Berkshire holds Occidental preferred shares and warrants [D08].
Berkshire cash position ~$146.7 billion at year-end 2021 [D08].
document_conflicts: Reported FCF $7.56bn vs company-defined FCF $8.809bn [D02, D04].

understandable.evidence: Occidental is a major oil and gas producer with well-defined, albeit commodity-dependent, operations in the Permian and global assets [D01].

durable_moat_and_pricing_power.evidence: The company maintains a low-cost position in the Permian, with well costs falling ~30% from 2019 to 2021 [D01].

consistent_earnings_record.evidence: While cyclical, the company demonstrates the ability to generate significant cash flow at normalized oil prices and showed operational discipline in 2021 [D01, D02].

high_roe_little_debt.evidence: Management is committed to aggressive deleveraging, having repaid $6.7 billion in debt in 2021 with a clear path to a $20bn net debt goal [D01].

capital_intensity.evidence: As a low-cost producer with a free-cash-flow yield of 18.5%, Occidental meets the criteria for a resource-advantaged commodity producer [D01, D04].

able_honest_owner_minded_management.evidence: CEO Vicki Hollub has demonstrated rational capital allocation by prioritizing debt reduction and shareholder returns over production growth [D01, D03].

size_moves_the_needle.evidence: With a market cap of $40.84bn, the company is sufficiently large to move the needle for Berkshire [D04].

price_screen.evidence: The free-cash-flow yield of 18.5% far exceeds 1.5x the 1.83% long bond yield, providing an ample margin of safety [D04].

conflicts_resolved: Reported FCF $7.56bn vs company-defined FCF $8.809bn → relied on $7.56bn as the more conservative figure provided in the valuation summary [D04].
gate1.one_line_business_quality_verdict: a low-cost Permian-focused oil and gas producer with disciplined management committed to deleveraging and high free cash flow generation

gate2.why_available: The market is wary of Occidental's historical leverage and the cyclical volatility of commodity prices [D02, D05]. We believe the market under-rates management's demonstrated discipline in debt reduction and the company's superior low-cost position in the Permian, which provides a significant margin of safety at an 18.5% free-cash-flow yield [D01, D04].
evidence: Management repaid $6.7 billion in debt during 2021 [D01].
Permian well costs declined ~30% from 2019 to 2021 [D01].
Free-cash-flow yield of 18.5% offers substantial value relative to the long bond [D04].
Company breaks even at $40 WTI, providing durability [D01].
gate2.market_narrative_we_disagree_with: The belief that high commodity prices are merely temporary or will inevitably lead to undisciplined capital allocation [D05].
what_must_be_true: Management continues to prioritize debt reduction over production growth
Permian assets maintain their low-cost competitive advantage
Oil prices remain at levels sufficient to support free cash flow generation above sustaining capital requirements

gate3.owner_earnings_per_share: Not in pack; assuming FCF as proxy of $8.10/share [D02, D04]
gate3.price_vs_value: Price $43.73 is ~62% of low-end; significant margin of safety
gate3.alternatives: T-bills/Cash yielding 1.83% [D04] are inferior to 18.5% FCF yield [D04]; buying Occidental provides superior capital allocation relative to low-yielding bonds.
gate3.downside_case: Commodity price crash to <$40 WTI; loss is not permanent provided debt reduction continues [D01].
flagged_assumptions: Maintenance capex assumed equal to reported sustaining capex of $3.9bn [D01]
FCF yield used as proxy for owner earnings yield [D02, D04]

gate4.role_description: permanent_passive_holder — value realised by the business compounding and rational capital allocation; Berkshire's edge is patience and permanent capital [D01].
value_realisation_path: Dividends and debt reduction increasing per-share value [D01], coupled with long-term compounding of the business's low-cost Permian assets [D01].
gate4.why_this_role_fits_the_era: As of 2022, Berkshire acts as a permanent, patient holder of equity in businesses we understand and trust to allocate capital rationally; Occidental’s focus on debt reduction and FCF generation fits our long-term investment horizon [D01, D03].

kill_criteria: Oil prices fall below $40/bbl for an extended period, preventing debt reduction [D01]
Management abandons disciplined capital allocation for aggressive debt-funded production growth [D01, D03]
Permian assets lose their relative cost-advantage compared to industry peers [D01]
gate5.berkshire_constraints: Must maintain a cash floor of at least $30B [D08]. Regulatory ownership thresholds apply to exceeding 10% [D08].
gate5.opportunity_cost: T-bills yielding 1.83% [D04] or existing high-quality holdings in the equity portfolio.
gate5.decider_reason: Occidental is an energy business of sufficient scale and understanding that allows for a significant position under Buffett's leadership.
gate5.biggest_risk_in_one_sentence: The inherent cyclicality of commodity prices could lead to volatility in earnings and cash flow, impacting the pace of required deleveraging.

drivers.driver: The company trades at an initial free-cash-flow yield of 18.5% compared to 1.83% for the long bond, representing a compelling margin of safety [D04].
Management led by Vicki Hollub has demonstrated exemplary capital discipline by prioritizing aggressive debt reduction, repaying $6.7 billion in 2021 [D01, D03].
Occidental possesses a low-cost competitive advantage in the Permian Basin, where well costs have declined by approximately 30% since 2019 [D01].
The business possesses structural durability with a cash flow break-even point of approximately $40 WTI, allowing it to generate significant cash across typical cycles [D01].

kill_criteria: Oil prices fall below $40/bbl for an extended period, preventing debt reduction [D01]
Management abandons disciplined capital allocation for aggressive debt-funded production growth [D01, D03]
Permian assets lose their relative cost-advantage compared to industry peers [D01]
final.what_would_change_our_mind: Evidence that management has shifted away from the debt-reduction mandate or that the structural cost-advantage of the Permian assets has been compromised by industry-wide changes or mismanagement.
final.memo:
Occidental is a major oil and gas producer with significant operations in the Permian Basin and globally, a business that we understand well after years of observing the energy industry [D01]. We have long held an interest in the company through our existing preferred shares and warrants, and the current operational performance confirms the strength of these underlying assets [D08].

The company maintains a formidable position as the largest acreage holder in the Permian Basin, where operational efficiency has improved dramatically, with well costs falling roughly 30% from 2019 to 2021 [D01]. This cost-advantaged position, combined with a break-even price of approximately $40 WTI, provides a durable foundation for generating cash flow through volatile commodity cycles [D01].

Under the leadership of Vicki Hollub, management has acted as true owners, prioritizing the reduction of debt over growth in production [D01, D03]. Their commitment was made clear in 2021 when they repaid $6.7 billion in debt, demonstrating the fiscal discipline necessary to steward capital effectively in a cyclical industry [D01].

The market currently appears fixated on commodity price volatility and historical leverage, offering us the opportunity to buy a cash-generating giant at a price that significantly undervalues its long-term potential [D02, D05]. With the company yielding 18.5% in free cash flow, we are acquiring a stream of earnings that compares favorably to any alternative available in the current interest rate environment [D04].

We value Occidental conservatively based on its normalized FCF, placing its intrinsic value between $70 and $90 per share [D03, D04]. At a share price of $43.73, we benefit from a substantial margin of safety while receiving an initial yield that is more than ten times the current long bond yield [D04].

Our primary risk remains the inherent volatility of oil prices, which could slow the necessary deleveraging process [D01]. However, provided the company continues to reduce debt and maintain its low-cost efficiency, we are content to act as permanent holders of this business [D01, D04].
